definition: The kernel is the part of the operating system that runs with full access to the hardware. It schedules processes, manages memory, and performs I/O on behalf of programs. User programs ask it to act through system calls instead of touching the hardware themselves.
details: Kernel space is the privileged address region. User space is where ordinary processes run, isolated from the hardware and from each other.
examples: The scheduler deciding which process runs next
The code that implements open, read, and write
